fatal_errors: The proposed DFT intervention does not reconstruct the high-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering method.
DFT can predict energetics and phase tendencies but cannot itself physically refine microstructure or densify the alloy.
The claimed percentage improvements are invented and unsupported by evidence or a defined metric.
No material composition, milling parameters, sintering window, FCC/BCC phase fractions, or quantitative mechanical targets from the target system are identified.
The proposed comparison against trial-and-error processing does not isolate or test the physical mechanism responsible for grain refinement and strengthening.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses phase stability and property prediction only at a generic computational level, whereas the target concerns physically processing equimolar CoCrFeNiTi powders by HEBM and SPS. It misses the argon milling conditions, vacuum sintering at 900–1000°C, nanocrystalline grain refinement, densification, mixed FCC/BCC structure, and Hall–Petch/dislocation/solid-solution strengthening mechanisms. Its boundary statement and falsification experiment are vague, and no evidence supports the numerical improvement claims. Although DFT could complement the target method by calculating phase energetics, it is neither the demonstrated processing method nor a sufficient mechanism for microstructure refinement and property optimization here.
